standard_prerequisites.name: Total variation distance of two laws on the positive integers
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 1704-1721 with the complete proof kept at 1723-1737
standard_prerequisites.statement: d_TV(mu,nu) = sup_A |mu(A) - nu(A)|, and for laws supported on N it equals sum_i (mu(i)-nu(i))^+ = sum_i (mu(i)-nu(i))^-.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the quantity the constructed coupling attains exactly; the identity form is proved inside this card rather than assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniform randomisation on the unit square
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given X of law mu and two independent uniforms U, U' on (0,1), the two-branch map f_{mu,nu}(X;U,U') changes value exactly when U*mu(X) > nu(X).
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the total variation identity into an explicit coupling with Y measurable with respect to (X,U,U'); verifying the law of Y is the second obligation.

core_obligations: Define the normalised partial sums z_j = sum_{i<=j} (mu(i)-nu(i))^- / d_TV(mu,nu) from the negative parts and the two-branch map f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) on N x (0,1)^2 (source 1747-1753).
Prove the defining equivalence f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) != m <=> a*mu(m) > nu(m) (1755-1760), which makes the change event {X != Y} computable and shows it has positive probability only when mu(m) > nu(m).
Identify P[X != Y] = P[U*mu(X) > nu(X)] with sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^+, hence with d_TV(mu,nu), using the counting-measure identity proved at 1723-1737.
Verify the second conclusion P[Y = n] = nu(n) by splitting on the two disjoint events that produce Y = n and normalising with sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^- = d_TV(mu,nu) (1785-1791).

proof_roadmap.step: Prove d_TV(mu,nu) = sum_i (mu(i)-nu(i))^+ = sum_i (mu(i)-nu(i))^- by comparing the signed measure xi = mu - nu with its positive set E.
Build the coupling map from the normalised partial sums z_j and prove the equivalence characterising the change event.
Compute P[X != Y] from the change event and the support of U, then compute P[Y = n] by splitting on the two disjoint events producing Y = n.

difficulty_reason: The claim is the existence of a coupling of two laws mu, nu on the positive integers with P[X != Y] exactly equal to d_TV(mu,nu) and with Y a function of X and two independent uniforms, so the proof must construct the coupling rather than invoke a metric. It defines the normalised partial sums z_j from the negative parts and a two-branch map f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) on N x (0,1)^2 (source 1747-1753), and the decisive step is the equivalence f_{mu,nu}(m;a,b) != m <=> a*mu(m) > nu(m) (1755-1760), which reduces the change event to {U*mu(X) > nu(X)}. Both conclusions are then computed exactly rather than estimated: P[X != Y] = sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^+ through the counting-measure identity proved at 1723-1737, and P[Y = n] = nu(n) by splitting on the two disjoint events producing Y = n and using sum_m (mu(m)-nu(m))^- = d_TV(mu,nu) (1785-1791).

dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: the public identity index (search terms maximal coupling, total variation distance, coupling, Arratia, Poisson-Dirichlet), the two same-source prepared cards, the 400 retired claims and the probability scouting notes for source 2516.

compared.actual_statement: source 200-207: existence of a coupling of the uniform random integer N_x with a parameter-one Poisson-Dirichlet process whose expected total l1 discrepancy is of order 1
compared.difference: The new claim is a general statement about two arbitrary laws on the positive integers; it names no random integer, no prime factor and no Poisson-Dirichlet process, and its proof (1715-1793) shares no span with 200-207. The same-source coupling uses this map at step 4 of line 488, so the lemma is an input of that theorem rather than a restatement of it.

That card bounds a Dirichlet boundary-event probability using a beta localization and a two-point Mecke argument at 1448-1628. The new claim is an exact coupling construction with an equality, not an estimate, and contains no Dirichlet or Poisson-Dirichlet object.
That card is an arithmetic boundary estimate over k-factorizations (1370-1446); the new claim is measure-theoretic and holds for any pair of laws on N.

editorial_notes: The lemma is attributed to Arratia in the source heading; the authors reproduce his proof at 1767-1793 and that reproduction is the proof carried here.
The supporting counting-measure identity 1715-1737 is included because the main proof invokes it at 1783; it is labelled as a supporting obligation and no separate count is assigned to it.
The map f_{mu,nu} is the same function the paper later uses to extract N_x (line 488); the context anchor 440-441 records that role without importing any part of the coupling theorem.
All displayed statements are taken from the fixed publisher source unchanged.
